justification: Fails IC1: Digital Twins are not discussed. Clearly meets EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

justification: The article focuses on cyber-physical systems, product-driven control, and hardware-in-the-loop simulation without any mention of Digital Twins. It explicitly mentions human-in-the-loop management (reducing frequency of human interventions), satisfying the human interaction aspect. However, it does not explicitly frame the system as a Digital Twin or discuss explainability per se. Given Phase 1’s high-recall aim and potential relevance, mark as maybe.

title: Framework for developing alternative reality environments to engineer large, complex systems
justification: The article proposes an XR framework for engineering design and human sensory experiences but does not mention or relate to Digital Twins. It fails IC1 and is clearly unrelated to Digital Twins (EC1), despite including human-centered aspects.

justification: The article is a systematic literature review (secondary study) on Construction 4.0, which falls under EC3 (secondary studies are excluded). Additionally, the abstract does not indicate Digital Twins as a central concept or discuss explainability/human interaction aspects.

title: Opportunities in intelligent modeling assistance
justification: The article focuses on intelligent modeling assistants and a conceptual reference framework for modeling, with no mention of Digital Twins. It fails IC1 and is clearly unrelated to Digital Twins (EC1), despite discussing human-centered aspects.

title: Moral control and ownership in AI systems
justification: The article focuses on AI ethics, moral agency, and general AI system architectures without any mention or clear relevance to Digital Twins. It fails IC1 (Digital Twin relevance). justification: Digital Twin is relevant (used to verify object poses with physics simulation), and the abstract mentions explainability/trust needs for robots. Given Phase 1’s high-recall objective, retain as potentially relevant.

justification: EC1: The article does not mention or discuss Digital Twins; it focuses on machine learning for tool wear monitoring in machining processes. There is also no indication of explainability, transparency, or human-interaction aspects.

justification: The article focuses on large-scale floor displays and human size perception in industrial visualization. It does not discuss Digital Twins, nor does it relate explainability or human interaction aspects within a Digital Twin context. Therefore, it fails IC1 and clearly violates EC1.

Given the high-recall Phase 1 and potential relevance to DT contexts, mark as maybe rather than exclude.

justification: The article centers on a DT-based framework for production scheduling using genetic algorithms, discrete-event simulation, and prognostics (EPHM) to compute failure probabilities. title: Model-Based Feature Information Network (MFIN): A Digital Twin Framework to Integrate Location-Specific Material Behavior Within Component Design, Manufacturing, and Performance Analysis
justification: Digital Twin is a central concept (framework enabling a DT description). While the abstract does not explicitly mention explainability or human-in-the-loop aspects, it emphasizes storing, searching, and retrieving contextual/lifecycle information, which may relate to transparency or human interaction in the full text. To maintain high recall, flag as potentially relevant for further screening.

title: Pitfalls and protocols of data science in manufacturing practice
justification: The article discusses data science frameworks for manufacturing and Industry 4.0 without mentioning Digital Twins. title: A multilayer multimodal detection and prediction model based on explainable artificial intelligence for Alzheimer’s disease
justification: The study focuses on an explainable AI model for Alzheimer’s diagnosis using SHAP and rule-based explanations, but it does not mention or relate to Digital Twins. Fails IC1 and clearly meets EC1 (unrelated to Digital Twins).

title: Artificial intelligence, cyber-threats and Industry 4.0: challenges and opportunities

While the explainability is not explicitly framed as XAI for Digital Twins, there is potential relevance to interpretability in a DT-integrated workflow. Given Phase 1’s high-recall aim and absence of clear exclusion criteria, it should be retained as a potential candidate.

justification: The article focuses on AI, blockchain, and wearable technology for chronic disease management without mentioning or discussing Digital Twins.
